axis_convention: Stored ages are in millions of years (Ma). Calibrated radiocarbon ages count back from 1950 CE and are stored as years before 1950 divided by 1,000,000. Other sources' ages in ka or kyr are stored as reported, divided by 1,000; their reference year is not stated by the sources and is not claimed to be 1950. No age is ever recomputed from today's date.

finds.title: Dinaledi Chamber fossils, Rising Star Cave, South Africa

find.context: the fossil deposit in the Dinaledi Chamber

claims.confidence: A bracket set by two dating methods. It is not a statistical range.
claims.text: The source brackets the time the fossils were laid down in the chamber between 335,000 and 236,000 years ago.
Fossil teeth, dated by combined uranium-series and electron-spin-resonance methods; and the oldest flowstone lying over the fossils, dated by the uranium–thorium method.

The older side of the bracket comes from the teeth, under the dating scenario the authors judge closer to conditions in the cave. The younger side comes from flowstone that formed over the fossils, so the fossils were already there.
This is the age of one deposit in one cave. It is not the span of time over which Homo naledi lived.

find.context: near the top of Member I of the formation

claims.confidence: 2σ, on the age of the eruption. It is not an uncertainty on the fossil's age.
claims.calibration: Kuiper et al. 2008. Under Renne et al. 2011 the same measurements give 234 ± 22.
claims.text: Omo I is older than a volcanic eruption dated 233,000 ± 22,000 years ago. The source calls this a minimum age for the fossil and gives no maximum.
claims.locator: Abstract; main text; corrected Supplementary Table 3

claims.text: Crystals of the mineral sanidine in pumice from the eruption, at Shala volcano in the Main Ethiopian Rift, dated by the argon–argon method. The fossil itself was not dated.
The source matches the eruption to an ash layer, the KHS Tuff, that lies above the level where Omo I was found, about 1.4 metres higher. A layer on top is younger than what lies under it.
The ± belongs to the eruption, not to the fossil. The source does not say how much older than the eruption the fossil is.

finds.title: Xiahe 2 rib, Baishiya Karst Cave, Tibetan Plateau

claims.confidence: The age range of layer 3 as the source reports and applies it. It is not a date on the rib.
claims.text: The rib comes from layer 3 of the cave, which the source dates to 48,000 to 32,000 years ago.
The layer's age comes from an earlier study of the cave's layers, which this source cites and applies. We have not read that earlier study.
The cave's layers, dated in the earlier study by optically stimulated luminescence and radiocarbon. The rib was not dated directly.
The rib was found in layer 3. The source adds that a chemical measure of protein ageing in the rib matches other bones from that layer.
The rib was identified from its proteins. This is the age of one layer in one cave.

finds.title: Bone fragment from the La Ferrassie 8 burial context, La Ferrassie, France

attributed_to.name: Neandertal
attributed_to.qualified: The 2020 authors judge the fragment most likely part of the La Ferrassie 8 child's skeleton. A 2023 study says that has not been demonstrated.

claims.confidence: The 95.4 % calibrated range. The ± on the radiocarbon measurement is the laboratory's own uncertainty and is a separate figure.
claims.text: A bone fragment was radiocarbon-dated directly. Calibrated, its date falls between 41,700 and 40,800 years before 1950, at 95.4 % probability.
The bone fragment itself, by radiocarbon: laboratory number ETH-99102, 36,170 ± 220 radiocarbon years BP, calibrated with IntCal20.
The date is on the find itself. The fragment was picked out by its proteins and grouped with Neandertals by its mitochondrial DNA.
The range is the uncertainty of one date on this fragment, not a length of time.

A later study models the age of the La Ferrassie 8 child at 44,900 to 39,900 years ago, at 95 % credibility. It keeps this fragment's date as an alternative for the child, if the fragment belongs to it, and says that has not been demonstrated. That model is for the individual, not a date on this fragment.
